name: Vanthorpe Analyst's Rule-Bend Daily Set
description: The Tier 4 specialist's quiet declaration of autonomy. A single-breasted blazer in deep teal-black hopsack — not quite a standard corporate color, but defensible as 'dark' in a dress code review. The cut is slightly longer in the rear than standard-issue, with a half-lining of copper-shot silk-analog that flashes when the wearer moves. Underneath, a Vanthorpe Coolweave dress shirt in pale oyster grey, collar open by exactly one button — the kind of studied informality that says 'I earned this.' The trousers are a slim, high-waisted cut in charcoal hopsack with a subtle herringbone texture, pressed with a sharp crease that does not require a machine. Aug-compatible split seams run along the outer thighs, finished with concealed magnetic closures for chrome leg accommodations; the seams are invisible when closed. Footwear is a pair of hand-burnished chestnut derbies with a crepe sole — comfortable enough for standing presentations, distinctive enough to be noticed in a meeting room. A brushed-gold minimalist watch, no corp branding, sits on the left wrist. One personal pin — small, abstract, origin unplaceable — on the left lapel. That pin is the entire personality budget for this outfit, and it is spent wisely.
functionality: Aug-compatible split seams with magnetic closure for chrome leg prosthetics, Coolweave fabric for passive temperature regulation during long hours, crease-retention trouser fabric, hidden interior chest pocket with RFID shielding
what_it_says: This person has been promoted at least once and intends to be promoted again. They follow the dress code but not the spirit of it — the teal-black, the open collar, the personal pin are all calibrated to signal individuality without triggering a dress code review. They know exactly how much they can get away with, and they enjoy knowing it.
worn_by: junior corponation executives on the way up
manufacturer: Vanthorpe Ready-to-Wear (blazer and trousers); Vanthorpe Ventline shirting; independent cobbler (footwear)
story_hooks: The single abstract pin on the lapel is a coded identifier for an underground labor organizing cell — worn openly because no one above Tier 3 knows what it means.

A Tier 5 executive notices the teal-black blazer in a meeting and asks where it's from — a small power test disguised as small talk. The answer determines whether the wearer gets a private project assignment or a lateral transfer.
The RFID-shielded chest pocket contains a data chip that was slipped to the wearer during a handshake — they don't know what's on it yet, but the person who gave it to them hasn't come back to work.

physical_description.visual_profile: A studied exercise in corporate restraint with calculated micro-rebellions. The silhouette reads 'senior analyst' at first glance—crisp, composed, intentionally muted—but rewards closer inspection. The teal-black blazer sits with subtle authority, its rear hem creating an almost duster-like shadow that breaks the rigid symmetry of standard corp wear. Movement reveals copper flash at the lining, a controlled hint of personality. The open collar and minimal jewelry suggest someone who has earned the right to bend, not break, the rules.
physical_description.fit: Slim and tailored through the torso with a half-lining that allows fluid movement. High-waisted trousers create a lengthened silhouette. The blazer falls slightly longer than regulation length—not flagrantly, but noticeably—with a cut that suggests custom tailoring rather than off-the-rack conformity. Comfortable enough for 12-hour workdays, deliberate enough to command a boardroom.
physical_description.primary_material: Deep teal-black hopsack wool-blend blazer; pale oyster grey Coolweave synthetic dress shirt; charcoal hopsack trousers with herringbone texture; hand-burnished chestnut leather derbies with crepe sole
physical_description.texture: Hopsack provides subtle surface texture without visual noise. Coolweave shirt has a soft, moisture-wicking finish. Trousers press to a knife-edge crease without mechanical aid—the fabric memory suggests quality weave. Leather derbies show intentional hand-burnishing, breaking the mirror-polish expectation of corporate footwear. Copper-shot silk-analog lining catches light with a controlled sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: deep teal-black (blazer, trousers) with pale oyster grey (shirt). Accent: brushed-gold watch case, chestnut leather (shoes). Hidden accent: copper-shot silk-analog lining flash on movement. Monochromatic foundation with micro-precious-metal details.
physical_description.closures: Standard button front on blazer (single-breasted, likely 2-3 buttons). Dress shirt buttons in pale grey or matte finish. Trousers with concealed magnetic closures on aug-compatible split seams along outer thighs—invisible when closed, accessible for chrome leg interfaces. Derbies with traditional leather lacing.
distinctive_features: Rear-hem extension on blazer (subtle, defensible, distinctive)
Copper-shot silk-analog half-lining visible on movement
Aug-compatible split seams with concealed magnetic closures (invisible closure tech)
Studied open-collar: exactly one button undone—calculated informality
Single abstract minimalist pin on left lapel (personality budget spent wisely)
Brushed-gold watch with no corp branding
Hand-pressed crease on trousers (no mechanical aid)
Herringbone texture on charcoal trousers (subtle visual interest)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 (working-class specialist with corporate proximity). The outfit signals someone who operates within the system but has earned enough autonomy to make micro-choices. Not wealthy enough for Tier 2 custom tailoring across all pieces, but invested enough to mix ready-to-wear basics with bespoke footwear and personal augmentation accommodations.
physical_description.cultural_context: A Tier 4 analyst, likely in data, logistics, compliance, or mid-level management. The outfit says: 'I understand the code, I follow most of it, and I've earned the right to bend the edges.' Aug-compatible seams indicate either current chrome augmentation or anticipated future modification. The pin is a quiet declaration of non-conformity—small enough to survive a dress code audit, distinctive enough to signal 'I have thoughts you won't find in the handbook.' This is someone operating at the boundary between corporate and autonomous identity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine, maintained, but not sterile. The hand-burnished shoes show intentional patina rather than scuffing. The crease in the trousers is sharp but lived-in. The blazer lining will show wear at the edges over time—a sign of daily use, not a flaw. The watch will accumulate the minor scratches of regular wear. This is an outfit designed to age gracefully, not to stay museum-perfect.
